Subject: How long should a water system last?
Preview: Buy right once, and you shouldn't be shopping again in five years.

---

Words I like;
Buy it nice, or buy it twice.
Here's a question I get asked a lot at the kitchen table: how long should a water system actually last?
The honest answer is decades, not years. A properly built system is mostly a tank, a control valve, and the right media inside. The tanks themselves routinely go 20 to 30 years. The valve is the part that does the work, and a quality valve should give you 10 to 15 years before it needs attention. The media (the stuff inside that actually treats your water) gets refreshed on its own schedule depending on what's in your water.
So if someone is selling you a system they expect to replace in five years, that tells you something about what they built.
If you already own one of ours, this is your reminder that you bought once and bought right. That was a smart call. Keep an eye on the valve down the road, stay on your media schedule, and it will quietly do its job for a very long time.
Longevity isn't luck. It's what you buy up front.
Not sure what you've got? Reply and I'll send you our free water assessment.
As promised, value in under a minute.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave

# Competitor Intel Brief — 2026-07-14

# Section 1 — Executive Summary

Only 3 of 8 competitor snapshots were provided this week (Mermaid Water, EcoWater, Hampton Roads Water Services); the other 5 are missing and should be re-pulled. Among those visible, Mermaid is the sharpest direct NoVA threat—running four stacked promos ($200 off heaters, $100 off first service, free Kinetico install, free heater flush) and bundling plumbing + water treatment under one roof. No competitor is publishing actual system pricing; everyone gates cost behind a "free water test," so the whole category competes on offer strength and trust signals, not transparent pricing. None of the three snapshots changed meaningfully from last week (prior snapshots are identical), so this is a quiet week—use it to move first.

# Section 2 — Per-competitor table

| Competitor | Hero positioning (one phrase) | Distinct services | Pricing visible? | Notable shift this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mermaid Water | "Local team that tests, installs correctly, and stands behind the work" | Water treatment + full plumbing, pumps/pressure, commercial (DI/RO), Kinetico dealer | No system prices; 4 dollar-value promos ($200, $100, free install, free flush) | No change vs. prior snapshot; promo stack still live |
| EcoWater | "Better Water Starts Here — global leader, nearly a century of expertise" | Softeners, filtration, smart-home/leak-detection, third-party certified systems, dealer network | No — "free water test," consult a Water Pro | No change vs. prior snapshot |
| Hampton Roads Water Services | "Your Full Service Water Quality Experts" (peace of mind) | Water testing, hard-water/bacteria/contaminant treatment, Lifetime Warranty, USA-made | No — free water test only | No change vs. prior snapshot |
| (5 others) | — data not provided — | — | — | Snapshots missing; re-request |

# Section 3 — Implications for ClearWave

- **Counter Mermaid's promo stack:** Test a limited-time, dollar-value new-customer offer (e.g., "$100 off first install" or "free heater flush with softener") since Mermaid is winning on concrete savings while ClearWave and others stay vague.
- **Borrow the "test-first" trust frame + strong warranty:** Both Mermaid ("we test first, explain clearly") and Hampton Roads (Lifetime Warranty) lead with credibility. Feature a free in-home water test CTA and a clearly named warranty above the fold.
- **Consider the plumbing + treatment bundle angle:** Mermaid's one-vendor-for-water-and-plumbing story is a real differentiator in NoVA; evaluate whether ClearWave can credibly position adjacent services or a maintenance plan to match it.

# Section 4 — Watch items

- **Re-pull the 5 missing competitor snapshots** — this week's brief is incomplete without them.
- **Mermaid:** promos are currently static; watch for expiration/refresh or any published pricing, and monitor commercial (DI/RO) push.
- **EcoWater:** smart-home/leak-detection line is the one place a competitor hints at a differentiated category — check if a local dealer surfaces pricing.
